# E2 release-health credentials (ruling 5)

E2's acceptance is: one command answers *did version N regress*. V10 has
merged, so a shipped binary stamps `git_sha` and `build_number` onto PostHog
super-properties and Crashlytics custom keys
(`app/lib/utils/build_provenance.dart`). What is missing is read access to
three production sources. Roadmap ruling 5 has sat open because "read-only
agent identity" is not a scope.

This file is the ask. It is not the integration. No API was called. No
credential on this host was opened. Nothing here authorizes a store-console
change.

Apps this would cover, from in-repo config (`codemagic.yaml`, `app/AGENTS.md`):

| Store | Identifier |
|---|---|
| App Store (prod) | bundle `com.friend-app-with-wearable.ios12`, ASC app id `6502156163` |
| Play (prod) | package `com.friend.ios` |
| Firebase Crashlytics (prod) | project `based-hardware-prod` |

Dev/TestFlight-dev identities (`*.development`, `com.friend.ios.dev`,
`based-hardware-dev`) are out of E2. Regression of a shipped version is a
prod-project question.

Do **not** reuse the existing App Store Connect `.p8` already in Codemagic
(`APP_STORE_CONNECT_PRIVATE_KEY` / `KEY_IDENTIFIER` / `ISSUER_ID`). That key
uploads and notarizes. E2 must not inherit upload.

---

## 1. App Store Connect — power and performance

### Credential

- **Mechanism:** App Store Connect API JWT (ES256), minted from a **Team**
  `.p8` + Issuer ID + Key ID. Not Sign in with Apple, not an Apple ID
  password, not the notarization key.
- **Role to mint the key:** Account Holder or Admin (Team keys). Individual
  keys can be generated by Account Holder, Admin, App Manager, Developer, or
  Marketing, and inherit that user's role. Whether a Developer-role key can
  actually `GET` power-and-performance is **unknown without a 403** (not
  tested). Third-party integrations that already call this API document an
  **App Manager Team key**; treat that as the conservative known-working
  role, not as Apple's published minimum.
- **One-time gate:** Account Holder must request App Store Connect API access
  in Users and Access → Integrations, if that has never been done for the
  team.
- **Object:** the one app `6502156163`. Prefer app-restricted key access if
  the console still offers it; otherwise the Team key sees every app in the
  account.
- **Scope string:** there is none. Apple roles are the scope.

### What David does

1. **Account Holder only:** Users and Access → Integrations → App Store
   Connect API → request access, if the team has no API access yet.
2. **Account Holder or Admin:** generate a **new** Team key named for E2
   (not the notarization key). Role: start at **App Manager**. Download the
   `.p8` once. Record Issuer ID and Key ID.
3. Anyone with the `.p8` can mint 20-minute JWTs after that. Rotating the
   key is the same people as step 2.

Console time if API access already exists: about ten minutes. If the
Account Holder must request API access first: that is a separate Apple
approval wait, duration **unknown**.

### Where it lives

Same local pattern as Codemagic's token on managed Macs:
`~/.config/omi/` (see `desktop/macos/docs/release.md` sourcing
`codemagic-env.sh`), files mode 600, never in git. Suggested names:
`asc-e2-key.p8`, with Key ID / Issuer ID in a sibling env file. If a later
scheduled GitHub Action needs it, it goes in a **repository or environment
secret** next to `CODEMAGIC_API_TOKEN` — not in `codemagic.yaml`'s
`appstore_credentials` group.

### Query that answers version N

Apple's **app** endpoint returns the **most recent versions only**:

```
GET https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com/v1/apps/6502156163/perfPowerMetrics
  ?filter[platform]=iOS
  &filter[metricType]=HANG
  &filter[deviceType]=all_iphones
Accept: application/vnd.apple.xcode-metrics+json
```

For a **named** version, use the build resource (ASC build UUID, not
Codemagic `BUILD_NUMBER`):

```
GET https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com/v1/builds/{asc-build-id}/perfPowerMetrics
  ?filter[platform]=iOS
  &filter[metricType]=HANG
```

`metricType=LAUNCH` is the startup number. Hang rate is the crash-adjacent
vital Apple actually vends here (terminations appear in the same family;
exact identifier for "crash-free" on this endpoint is **unknown without a
response body**). Values are percentiles (p50 / p90) plus a
`deltaPercentage` against `referenceVersions`. Grain is **app marketing
version** (and optionally a specific ASC build), not a calendar day and not
`git_sha`. Sample delay is typically a day-plus; whether a given build has
enough opted-in MetricKit samples is **unknown**.

Join to a commit: marketing version + ASC build → Codemagic
`BUILD_NUMBER` / V10 `build_number` is **not documented as 1:1**. V10
`git_sha` is not an ASC field.

### Without credentials

Nothing from this source. Local git cannot see hang rate or launch time.

## 2. Play vitals — Developer Reporting API

### Credential

- **Mechanism:** Google Cloud **service account** JSON key (or, later,
  Workload Identity Federation — the repo already uses WIF for some GCP
  deploys; do not invent a second pattern).
- **Google API scope:** `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/playdeveloperreporting`
- **Play Console permission (the real one):** **View app information
  (read-only)** on app `com.friend.ios`. That is what
  `vitals.crashrate` and `vitals.anrrate` document. Not Finance, not
  Release to production, not "Admin (all permissions)".
- **GCP extras:** enable *Google Play Developer Reporting API* on the GCP
  project that owns the SA. No Play↔Cloud linking is required (Google
  removed that).
- **Object:** one Play app, `com.friend.ios`. Grant app access, not account
  access, when inviting the SA.

### What David does

1. GCP: create SA `omi-e2-play-vitals@<project>.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.
   Creating SAs is an IAM-admin action; if David is the GCP Owner that is
   him. No other GCP roles are required for Play (the permission lives in
   Play Console).
2. Enable the Play Developer Reporting API on that GCP project.
3. Create one JSON key (or skip the key and use WIF if this will only run
   as GitHub Actions).
4. **Play Console Account Owner or Admin:** Users and permissions → Invite
   new users → paste the SA email → app `com.friend.ios` only → permission
   **View app information (read-only)** → Invite. First-time SA invites are
   an Owner/Admin step; David if he is the Play account owner.

Console time: about 15 minutes if he is both GCP Owner and Play Account
Owner. Two consoles if those hats sit on different people — **unknown**.

### Where it lives

JSON key: under the same `~/.config/omi/` directory as `codemagic-env.sh`,
mode 600, a vitals key file (do not invent a repo path for it). GitHub:
environment/repository secret, same as
`CODEMAGIC_API_TOKEN`. Do not put it in Codemagic mobile signing groups.
Prefer WIF over a long-lived JSON key if the only consumer is Actions;
the laptop command still needs a key or `gcloud` ADC, which contributors
will not have — and must not need (E2 without credentials still has to
run).

### Query that answers version N

Crash-free (actually crash **rate**) per Android `versionCode`, per day
(PST):

```
POST https://playdeveloperreporting.googleapis.com/v1beta1/apps/com.friend.ios/crashRateMetricSet:query
Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN
{
  "timelineSpec": {
    "aggregationPeriod": "DAILY",
    "startTime": { "year": Y, "month": M, "day": D, "timeZone": "America/Los_Angeles" },
    "endTime":   { "year": Y, "month": M, "day": D2, "timeZone": "America/Los_Angeles" }
  },
  "dimensions": ["versionCode"],
  "metrics": ["userPerceivedCrashRate", "crashRate", "distinctUsers"]
}
```

ANR:

```
POST https://playdeveloperreporting.googleapis.com/v1beta1/apps/com.friend.ios/anrRateMetricSet:query
```

same body, metrics `userPerceivedAnrRate`, `anrRate`, `distinctUsers`.

**Regression field:** `userPerceivedCrashRate` (share of distinct users with
at least one foreground crash in the period). Compare versionCode `N` to
`N-1` on the same days once both have enough `distinctUsers` (Play rounds
that count; a tiny cohort is not a rate). Grain is **per day ×
versionCode**. `versionCode` is the Play integer; Codemagic's
`BUILD_NUMBER` is what V10 stamps as `build_number`, and is what Play
usually receives as versionCode — **treat as likely-same, not proven**.
There is no `git_sha` dimension.

Slow-start exists (`vitals.slowstartrate`) if E2 later wants launch time on
Android; not required to unblock crash/ANR.

### Without credentials

Nothing from this source.

## 3. Crashlytics — BigQuery export (not a Crashlytics read API)

The Firebase Crashlytics dashboard has no agent-queryable read API that
this program should depend on. The roadmap already picked the export.
Flutter Crashlytics in this app is `4.3.2` (`app/pubspec.yaml`), which
clears the sessions-export SDK floor (Flutter ≥ 3.4.5).

### Credential (two layers)

**A. Enable the export** (once, no agent identity):

- Firebase console → Project settings → Integrations → BigQuery → Link,
  on **`based-hardware-prod`**.
- Permission: `firebase.links.create` / `firebase.links.update` —
  **Owner or Firebase Admin**. Editor is not enough.
- Tick **Crashlytics**. Tick **Include sessions** (without it you get
  crash events and no crash-free denominator). Streaming export is
  optional (Blaze-only); batch is enough for "did version N regress".
- First batch can take **up to 48 hours**. Backfill is at most 30 days.

**B. Query identity** (the agent):

- GCP SA with **`roles/bigquery.dataViewer` on dataset
  `firebase_crashlytics`** (and `firebase_sessions` if sessions export is
  on), plus **`roles/bigquery.jobUser` on the project** so it can run
  jobs. Not `roles/firebase.admin`, not project Viewer, not the
  Crashlytics service-agent role.
- Object: those two datasets in the GCP project behind
  `based-hardware-prod`. Dataset-level Data Viewer is narrower than
  project-level.

### What David does

1. **Owner or Firebase Admin:** link BigQuery, enable Crashlytics +
   sessions, leave GA/other product exports off if the wizard offers a
   per-product toggle.
2. GCP IAM: mint SA `omi-e2-crashlytics-bq@…`, grant the two roles above.
   Dataset IAM can be done by a dataset owner; creating the SA is IAM
   admin.
3. JSON key or WIF, same storage rule as Play.

Console time: 15–20 minutes if he is Firebase Owner on
`based-hardware-prod`. Then wait up to 48 hours before the first useful
query. Whether that project is already linked to BigQuery is **unknown**.

### Where it lives

Identical to Play: `~/.config/omi/` or a GitHub secret. One SA can hold
both Play invite and BQ Data Viewer if David wants a single E2 identity;
two SAs are cleaner (Play cannot be scoped with GCP IAM). Prefer two.

### Query that answers version N

Crashlytics custom keys from V10 are `custom_keys.key` /
`custom_keys.value` (`git_sha`, `build_number`). Tables are per app, dots
to underscores, for example `firebase_crashlytics.com_friend_ios_ANDROID`
and `…com_friend_app_with_wearable_ios12_IOS` — exact table names are
**unknown until the dataset exists**.

Crash-free sessions, once `firebase_sessions` is exporting, is a join of
session rows to crash rows on installation/session id, filtered on
`build_number` or `git_sha`. Exact sessions schema column for the V10
keys is **unknown without the dataset**. Until sessions export is on, you
can count crash events per `build_number` but you **cannot** honestly
report a crash-free *rate* (no denominator).

Grain: **per event timestamp** (batch table is daily sync). You can
aggregate per `build_number` or per `git_sha` — that is the only of the
three sources that answers "this commit". Compare N to the previous
shipped `build_number`.

### Without credentials

Still no production rates. What V10 *does* give offline is the **join
key**: any crash row that someday appears will carry `git_sha` /
`build_number`. The command can already print, from git, what those
values would be for HEAD.

---

## What the command can answer with no credentials

| Question | Answerable now? |
|---|---|
| What `git_sha` / `build_number` would this checkout stamp? | Yes. `app/scripts/build_provenance_dart_defines.sh` (SHA from `git rev-parse HEAD`, build `local` unless `BUILD_NUMBER` / `OMI_BUILD_NUMBER` / a `v*+N` tag is in the environment). |
| Did shipped version N regress crash-free / ANR / hang / launch? | **No.** Those numbers are not in git. |
| Map store version N → commit | **Not from git alone.** Store binaries ignore `pubspec.yaml`; Codemagic assigns `BUILD_NUMBER`. Tags of the form `vX.Y.Z+N` would help; whether mobile production tags exist in that shape is **unknown** (desktop uses `v*-macos`). Calling Codemagic to resolve a build id is a credential (`CODEMAGIC_API_TOKEN`) and is out of "no credentials". |
| Capture-success or sign-in success for version N | **No**, and not one of these three sources. Those are PostHog / F1. Agents in this program must not call PostHog. |
| Read a Crashlytics CSV someone already downloaded | Only if a human drops a file on disk. Not an API, not in the repo, not a substitute for the export. |

A no-credential E2 therefore reports provenance identity and
`regression: unknown`. That is still a real command: it fails closed
instead of pretending the stores were queried.

---

## Decision (David)

**Minimum grant that unblocks a useful E2:** enable Crashlytics → BigQuery
export **with sessions** on `based-hardware-prod`, and a dataset-scoped
`bigquery.dataViewer` + project `bigquery.jobUser` service account. That
is the only source that can use V10's `git_sha`. Play and ASC answer
rates by `versionCode` / marketing version and still need a second hop to
a commit.

**Cost to him:** one Firebase Owner session, ~15–20 minutes, then up to
48 hours of empty tables. No App Store Connect API request. No Play
invite. No new GitHub workflow.

**Still impossible after that grant:** iOS hang/launch (ASC), Android
ANR/crash-free *as Play computes them* (Play has the usage denominator
Crashlytics only gets if sessions export is on — different definition),
capture-success, sign-in success, and any claim about a version that
shipped before the export's 30-day backfill.

**Play + ASC on top:** another ~25 minutes split across Play Account
Owner and Apple Account Holder/Admin, plus a second secret family, plus
the risk of handing agents a key that must not be the notarization `.p8`.
Worth it when E2 is the thing unblocking H3 and a halt decision. It is
not the thing unblocking this lane this week.

**Recommendation: do not provision Play or App Store Connect for E2 yet.
Do the Crashlytics BigQuery export if you are in the Firebase console
anyway; otherwise let E2 wait.**

The rest of the Product-infra build queue is blocked on C7 landing (C8,
F3, F1, F2) or on hub hardware (G1/G2 via Spine B). H3 waits on E2, but
H3's useful intake is "a crash cluster joined to a commit" — which is
exactly the BigQuery export — and "vitals / store reviews," which need
Play and ASC. Shipping a halt-quality vitals command before F1 exists
duplicates the Play/ASC consoles and still cannot answer capture-success.
V10 already did the only in-repo half of E2. Spending Account Holder time
on two store APIs now, while C7 is still a pending skeleton, is the wrong
place to spend it.

If you do one console action from this file, it is: Firebase
`based-hardware-prod` → Integrations → BigQuery → Link → Crashlytics +
Include sessions.

---

## Unknowns (would require an API or a console that was not opened)

- Whether `based-hardware-prod` is already linked to BigQuery, on Blaze,
  or already exporting Crashlytics/sessions.
- Exact BigQuery table names and whether `git_sha` / `build_number`
  custom keys are present on sessions rows as well as crash rows.
- Whether a Developer-role ASC key can `GET` `perfPowerMetrics` (403).
- Whether the team has already requested App Store Connect API access.
- Whether Play `versionCode` equals Codemagic `BUILD_NUMBER` for every
  production track.
- ASC crash-free field name inside the xcode-metrics payload; sample
  delay for Omi's population.
- Who is Play Account Owner vs Firebase Owner vs Apple Account Holder if
  they are not the same person.
- Whether mobile production git tags encode `+BUILD_NUMBER`.
- Any live crash-free or ANR number for a current version.

Public docs used (fetched as pages, not as authenticated APIs): Apple
App Store Connect API help and `perfPowerMetrics` endpoints; Google Play
Developer Reporting `vitals.crashrate` / `vitals.anrrate`; Firebase
Crashlytics BigQuery export and dataset schema; Firebase
`firebase.links.create` role table.
